what_happened: The route said turn RIGHT, but the ego went straight in its lane, about 5.6 m off the recorded path, behind lead car 9, which was slowing for a red light. The ego braked only gently, from 12.2 to 4.8 m/s. The gap shrank from 14.5 m to 4.4 m, and the ego's front hit car 9 at 10.0 s, before anything struck its rear.

With a RIGHT command, the ego drifted about 7 m left of the recorded path, which kept to the right lanes. It held about 8.5 m/s straight at a bus (127) that was turning out of the cross street into the ego's new lane and coming toward it. The gap closed about 14 m/s from 46 m, so the bus was moving toward the ego, and the ego hit it head-on while barely slowing (8.9 → 7.5 m/s).

With a RIGHT command and the recorded path veering right, the ego went the other way and steered left across several lanes, ending up 8.3 m off the recording. That put it in the path of bus 127, which was turning out of the cross street and coming down those left lanes toward the ego. The ego only slowed from 8.0 to 5.9 m/s and hit the bus head-on.

The command was RIGHT and the route went right, but after handoff the ego steered left, away from the route, and cut across the lanes toward the left curb. Its front hit the bus (actor 127) in the left lanes at about 4 m/s, when the ego was about 8 m off the recorded human path.

On approach to a red light, with a RIGHT command, the ego stayed in the lane left of the recorded path (about 6.4 m off it) and closed on car 9, which was nearly stopped ahead in its lane. The ego slowed from 11.8 to 4.3 m/s, but the gap shrank from 18.5 m to 4.7 m and its front hit car 9's rear at 10.1 s, so it braked too late and too gently.

The route command was RIGHT, but the ego drifted left of the recorded path, about 8 m off by the end. A bus (127) turned from the cross street into the lanes ahead and ended up in the ego's lane. The ego was clearly able to see the bus in the camera from 7.2s, but it only slowed from about 8.9 to 7.4 m/s and drove its front into the bus at 9.2s.

The route said turn RIGHT, but the ego stayed in a lane about 5 m left of the recorded right-turn path. There it closed on lead car 9, which was slowing for a red light. The ego braked from 12 to 5.4 m/s, but the gap still shrank from 14.8 m to 4.5 m, and the ego's front hit car 9's rear at 10.0 s.

Approaching a red light at the intersection, the ego was slowing (13.6 to 6.1 m/s) but not hard enough. The gap to lead car 9, stopping in the ego's lane at the stop line, closed from 30.7 m to 4.5 m, and the ego hit its rear with its front bumper; the earlier camera frames showed the car and the red light clearly.

The route command was RIGHT and the recorded path stayed to the right, but the policy steered left across lanes, ending up about 10 m off the recorded path. That put it in the path of bus 127, which was turning through the intersection into those left lanes. The ego braked late, slowing from 8.6 to 4.7 m/s, and hit the bus with its front at 9.8 s.

The route said RIGHT and the recorded path went into the right-turn lane, but the ego stayed about 6 m to the left, in the straight lane, behind car 9. Car 9 was slowing to a stop at the stop line for a red light. The ego slowed from 12.5 to 4.9 m/s, but too late: the gap closed from 33.7 m to 4.5 m and the ego's front hit car 9 at 9.9 s.

The route said RIGHT and the human drove in the right lanes, but the ego stayed in the far-left lane, about 10 m off the recording. Bus 127 was clearly visible from 7.6 s as it swung out of the intersection into that lane ahead. The ego only slowed from 8.4 to 5.5 m/s and hit the bus with its front at 9.6 s. Its planned path only swerved left at the last moment. Being rear-ended came after the front collision.

The command was RIGHT, but the policy kept the ego in a left-side lane and planned a path that curved further left, well away from the recorded right-turn path. It slowed from 12.6 to 7.7 m/s and drove onto the raised median island ahead of the intersection, about 7.8 m off the human trajectory, without hitting any actor.
